# The Sky That Remembers Every Star

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit." — Psalm 147:4–5 (NIV)

## Reflection
Step outside on an October evening and look up. On a clear night far from city lights, you can see perhaps two or three thousand stars. Yet astronomers estimate our galaxy alone holds over a hundred billion—and the observable universe contains more galaxies than there are grains of sand on every beach on Earth.

Here is the astonishing thing: God numbers them all. Not approximately. Not statistically. He counts each one and names each one. The same God who spoke galaxies into being also knows the hairs on your head and the quiet worries you carried into today.

In the fall, as the Pleiades rise in the east and Orion climbs over the horizon, we're watching ancient light—some of it traveling toward us for thousands of years before reaching your eyes tonight. And the One who set those photons in motion before your ancestors were born has never once lost track of a single one.

If God holds the stars in their places and calls them by name, how much more does He hold you? Your name is not forgotten in the vastness. You are not a random speck in an indifferent cosmos. You are known, counted, and called by the God who made it all.

## Prayer
Lord of the stars, thank You for numbering and naming what we cannot even count. When the night feels vast and we feel small, remind us that Your understanding has no limit and Your care has no bounds. Help us rest tonight beneath a sky that declares Your faithfulness. In Jesus' name, Amen.
